text: I bought a property. When I first opened the door, I was so disappointed that I stood and didn't enter. But I did move in, knowing that I would be renovating this place. Because I was so disappointed, or maybe just tired, I didn't know what I wanted to see the construction go exactly, or all the tiling and painting and floors. I just got sick of having rooms that are very small and cramped and dark. I didn't really want to look into the details of what would the kitchen look like or what color would the walls be. I just wanted something light, light and light. That's it. It's very simple. And then the construction started. It is always very noisy, so loud. And the walls come down. And when you come down the walls, you see the old walls. There were different wallpapers and layers and layers of people who lived there before. And it is very nice to see that. It is very emotional. So I think that renovation is very nice. But also I was living in this house during the construction, and it was very challenging. I just ate dinner every day in the box on a chair. And everything was plastic covered. And then after I went to bed at night, everything was covered with dust. Dust everywhere. Dust in my hair, in my books, in my phone. I just used to say, this is the past that I am sanding away. This is the past that is making this dust that I am seeing. So it was very very emotional. And I think it is also kind of romantic to see all the dust that comes from the different walls and different ceilings that you are sanding and demolishing. But at the same time it's very challenging. Because you need to just keep going, keep demolishing, keep sanding. But it never looks good until the very last, like 80% of the renovation is done. And at some point, the renovation looks beautiful, and then it goes down again. Like that two weeks before I moved in, it looked horrible. I was just like, this is terrible, I don't want to move in here. And then the very last weekend, it looked perfect, so I moved in. But during that process, it's very challenging to see the results that come with the designs. The tiles that you select and the color of the walls and everything. You don't see it for a very long time. There are delays, there are problems. So you have to really, really just commit to what you want and keep going. And then there are a lot of decisions that are small, but they are very big. Choosing a very small detail of the grout or the tiles or the walls. Which color I want, which white I want. Which gray I want. So these decisions feel very important and very difficult. And then I did it. And now I very much love what I have. Very simple design. I have light oak floor. I love it very much. I also love the color of my kitchen cabinet. It's a green. And I love my white tiles in the bathroom, very simple. And now I very much love what I see. I think it is very nice. And when I open the door, I very much love this house. It doesn't make me disappointed anymore. And I think the renovation changed my life in the sense that I pay attention to different things. And I like the house very much. And this is exactly what I wanted. I think that before I was very skeptical about it. And I now very much like having the house that I know from inside, that I know how I used the space, that I like it, that I really wanted to design it. And I think this is very nice. So I'm very happy with the result. And what I want to keep in mind is that it's not finished. I think it's important to remember that renovation is never finished. It's never perfect. So I want to always remember that things will scratch, things will stain. Things will age. And that's ok. This is how life is. I don't want to make my home perfect and clean and museumy. I want it to live. I want to age it. I want it to be my own. And I want the scratches. I want the stains. I want the use and the life that will come. That's what I want. And that's what I have. And I think in the future I will scratch the floor. And I already scratched it very lightly. And it was very nice to see because it means I really live here. And I very much like this.
